source_documents.title: How Inter- and Intramolecular Processes Dictate Aggregation Induced Emission in Crystals Undergoing Excited State Proton Transfer

reference_evidence_units.quote: compound 2 is dark in both solution and the solid state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The target is the non-emissive negative-control compound, not an AIE turn-on emitter.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Reported experimental phenotype from reference 41; labels below explain quenching rather than enhancement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: in 2 the dominant motif is the face to face π-π stacking of chromophores.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Compound 2 has face-to-face stacking distinct from compound 1's herringbone packing.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No value measured for compound 1 is assigned to compound 2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: There is no signiﬁcant intermolec- ular charge transfer upon excitation in either material.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Vertical-excitation calculations show no substantial intermolecular CT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Does not exclude charge redistribution within each molecule.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For 2, oscillator strengths from E* are extremely small.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The relaxed E* dimer state is effectively dark and delocalized; Table 1 gives oscillator strengths 0.002 and 0.000 for parallel/antiparallel dimers.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Table visually inspected. E* is not stable in vacuum or monomer models, so this is a dimer-specific result.

reference_evidence_units.quote: radiative mechanisms alone cannot ex- plain the negligible quantum yield of 2.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The localized single-proton-transfer K* state retains appreciable oscillator strength, so purely radiative suppression is insufficient.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The doubly transferred dark K* state lies above bright FC and is not assumed to dominate.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For 2, the S1-S0 MECI is classically accessible with a barrier of 0.4 eV from the K* minimum.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: After bright-state excitation, the keto CI remains energetically accessible in compound 2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is residual CI access and nonradiative quenching, not successful restriction that causes AIE.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the accessibility of the MECI in 2 is aided by the short-range electrostatic interactions with the surrounding molecules.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Crystal electrostatics stabilizes compound 2's MECI relative to S1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Mechanical-only embedding puts both compounds' MECIs above the populated state; electrostatic treatment is consequential.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the larger stabil- ity of the MECI for 2 is mainly explained by the electronic eﬀects provided by the methoxy substituent
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Methoxy substitution, assisted by crystal electrostatics, favors CI deactivation despite packing restrictions.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Do not infer this substituent effect from unverified legacy SMILES; attribution uses source compound 2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The π-π stacking interactions in 2 increase the excitonic coupling.
reference_evidence_units.subject: Compound 2 (methoxy-substituted 2'-hydroxychalcone derivative)
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Same source computational protocol as compound 1; non-emissive compound 2 in solution and crystal.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Stronger excitonic coupling and delocalized E* character provide an additional nonradiative route relative to compound 1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The source also requires localized ESIPT/K* CI deactivation; coupling alone is not a complete explanation.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Crystal packing changes distortion possibilities and short-range electrostatics stabilizes the nonradiative channel.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The calculated single-proton-transfer keto state leads to the accessible CI; proton transfer is part of quenching rather than proof of bright emission.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Face-to-face excitonic interactions produce a dark delocalized E* channel; the source regards it as contributory, not sufficient.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Dark E* versus still-bright K* oscillator strengths explicitly distinguish state channels; radiative differences alone cannot explain the near-zero yield.

reference_mechanisms.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The broad family includes CI-mediated nonradiative decay: compound 2 retains access and remains dark. This must not be rendered as RACI-induced enhancement.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Steric hindrance does not shut the operative K* CI. No independent harmonic RIM explanation of the target's behavior is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific CT or TICT mechanism is established in this extraction.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No photoinduced electron-transfer quenching or turn-on is established; energy transfer and CT character are not by themselves PET.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No operative target-specific triplet or metal-mediated pathway is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The broad family includes CI-mediated nonradiative decay: compound 2 retains access and remains dark. This must not be rendered as RACI-induced enhancement.

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No higher-singlet-state emission or anti-Kasha mechanism is established; higher-state absorption alone is insufficient.
